Fills rather than dosage units, because the CMS unit count mixes six presentations (75 mg, 150 mg syringe, 150 mg pen, 300 mg pen and the intravenous concentrate), so a unit is not a comparable quantity across the file; claims are. The case for far lower: SERENA, Novartis's own 5-year observational study in 1,740 plaque psoriasis patients, reports retention of 88.5%, 76.3%, 68.6%, 63.1% and 58.5% at years 1 to 5 (Dermatology and Therapy 2026;16:2837-2856, doi:10.1007/s13555-026-01722-0), which compounds to about 10% a year. Two things separate them. SERENA enrolled patients already on secukinumab for 16 weeks or more, so it never sees the early dropouts, and it measures a cohort's persistence rather than the share of a calendar year a treated Medicare patient is actually dispensed drug. It is the second that pairs with a per-beneficiary price. Read 0.505 as time on drug inside a year, not as the probability a patient abandons the brand

column12: stated equal to the incidence on purpose, which makes the pool the year's own diagnoses rather than an accumulating stock. PMR is treated as a course - REPLENISH is 52 weeks on a 24-week steroid taper - and most patients come off treatment. The alternative reading is the published point prevalence, 6 per 1,000 persons aged 50 and over on 1 January 1992 (Salvarani C et al., Arthritis Rheum 1995;38(3):369-373, doi:10.1002/art.1780380311), which on the same 123,327,950 is 739,968 people and implies an average disease duration of 9.4 years. That prevalence counts everyone carrying a PMR diagnosis and alive on the date, including those long off glucocorticoids, so it is not the treatable pool. Taking the diagnoses rather than the stock is the conservative choice and it is roughly a tenth of the alternative; a reader who prefers the stock should read this layer about nine times larger

column11: as the prevalence row: the book treats a year's diagnoses as the pool for an indication given as a course (Raheel S et al., Arthritis Care Res 2017, doi:10.1002/acr.23132)

the share of PMR patients who flare while glucocorticoids are tapered, which is what the indication requires. The European Commission approved Cosentyx on 21 October 2026 for adults with PMR 'who had inadequate response to glucocorticoids or relapse during glucocorticoid taper' (Novartis media release of that date), and REPLENISH (NCT05767034) required 'at least one episode of PMR relapse while attempting to taper prednisone at a dose that is >= 5 mg/day ... within the past 12 weeks'. A systematic literature review of 11 prospective glucocorticoid-tapering studies in PMR (nine randomised trials and two longitudinal cohorts) reports 'Flare rates were generally high (57-100%) and did not appear to differ according to tapering speed' (Rheumatology (Oxford) 2026;65:keag056, doi:10.1093/rheumatology/keag056). 0.57 is the bottom of that range
column12: the low end of a published 57% to 100% range is taken, and the range is wide because flare definitions differ between the trials in it. At the top of the range the eligible pool is 78,807 rather than 44,920. Nothing further is deducted for diagnosis or referral: PMR is usually managed in primary care on prednisone and a specialist referral filter would belong here, but no US share for it was found, so it sits inside the penetration judgement instead

column11: a judgement. Cosentyx would be the second biologic approved in the United States for this exact population: KEVZARA (sarilumab) is already indicated for 'adult patients with polymyalgia rheumatica who have had an inadequate response to corticosteroids or who cannot tolerate corticosteroid taper' (BLA 761037, label effective 2026-02-27, openFDA), and tocilizumab is used off-label on the strength of SEMAPHORE. Against that, REPLENISH met its primary endpoint and all secondaries, with sustained remission at week 52 in 41.2% on 300 mg and 40.6% on 150 mg against 20.4% on placebo (Stone JH et al., N Engl J Med 2026;395:637-647, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2602567, 381 patients randomised 1:1:1), and Cosentyx is a familiar subcutaneous product in rheumatology where Kevzara's IL-6 blockade carries a different safety conversation. 15% of the relapsing pool at peak
column12: the number to argue with. The case for more: most PMR is still managed on prednisone alone and both biologics are expanding a market rather than splitting a fixed one. The case for less: a 72-year-old median age at diagnosis means a Medicare population and a prior-authorisation fight against a $10 generic, and PMR is diagnosed and treated largely outside rheumatology
